whatContradictedTheCard.contradiction: The card's/scout's join key (WCAD `propertyid`, crosswalked through a second WCAD Parcels/geometry dataset `an3x-cnmw`) is wrong. Live-verified: `propertyid` does not match txgio_parcel.prop_id's format at all. The real join key is WCAD's `quickrefid` field, which is in the identical "R"+digits format as txgio_parcel.prop_id for Williamson and was confirmed live (5/5 sampled values matched real txgio_parcel rows with correct addresses). This makes the rail a pure attribute join with NO spatial component and NO second WCAD dataset needed at all -- simpler than the card described, not just differently sourced.

The card claimed a literal `agflag` field distinguishes ag-qualified records. Live full-sweep (305,879 rows) found `agflag` sparse and unreliable: 37 real D-coded (ag-qualified) rows carry `agflag='L'` not `'Y'`, and both live D2-coded rows carry no `agflag` key at all. The rail derives `ag_flag` from `statecode` starting with "D" instead, which is reliable on every row.

The card names one URL (TWDB's Public_Utility_Commission_CCN_Water MapServer) and says CCN_NO's leading digit splits water=1/sewer=2 within that source. Live-verified: that source is 100% water/exempt (TYPE=1), zero sewer rows. The leading-digit rule is real but only fires across two combined sources; the sewer counterpart (a separate ArcGIS Online FeatureServer, services6.arcgis.com/N6Lzvtb46cpxThhu/.../Sewer_CCN_Service_Areas/FeatureServer/230, 967 rows) was not named in the card and was found via independent search.

The TWDB water source's advancedQueryCapabilities report supportsPagination:false, and a query using resultOffset/resultRecordCount returns a hard 400 error -- the card did not flag this. Keyset pagination (WHERE oid > cursor ORDER BY oid ASC, no resultRecordCount) was required and confirmed live-working instead.

The card did not flag that the TEA ArcGIS layer's native spatial reference is NAD_1983_Lambert_Conformal_Conic (a projected CRS in meters), not WGS84. Every query passes outSR=4326 explicitly; omitting it would have silently misaligned every polygon against txgio_parcel's SRID 4326 geometry.

Operational, not a sourcing error: TWDB's own ArcGIS Web Adaptor is intermittently returning an HTML "Could not access any server machines" page instead of JSON under this session's own querying (reproduced twice via the wired CLI and independently a third time via raw curl with no code involved). Retry/backoff logic is built for this; it is named here because a Cloud Run --apply execution of factory-acquire-utility-ccn may need a manual retry if it lands in this window, which is a real operational risk the card's cited sources gave no reason to expect.

scratch.text: This program's writer-allowlist encodes a real architectural rule via the liveRest field, not just documentation: every existing writer job has liveRest:false, and requireEasementNoLiveRest actively refuses liveRest!==false for that one job. Reading the allowlist file directly (not just the AGENT_CONTRACT prose) surfaced that no writer job in this repo calls a live external API at write time -- which is why this wave needed a two-layer acquire/write split at all, not a design preference.

A prior scouting pass's cited join key can be wrong in a way that only shows up by fetching a live sample and cross-checking format against the actual target table, not by re-reading the scout's prose more carefully. agValuation's propertyid-vs-quickrefid error would have shipped a rail that joined against nothing.

ArcGIS FeatureServer/MapServer instances vary meaningfully in capability even within one card: native CRS (TEA projected, PUCT sewer Web Mercator, others WGS84), pagination support (TWDB explicitly refuses resultOffset with a named error; TEA accepts it fine), and field-name conventions. Querying each source's own ?f=json metadata live, per source, before writing its acquire script, caught all of these; trusting a single documented pattern across sources would not have.

Attempting to validate a write job's real SQL locally before its acquire job has run --apply against production is not possible -- the zone-major hoist queries the staging table directly and errors 'relation does not exist' rather than returning zero rows. Do not attempt a write-job dry-run before its paired acquire job has landed at least once.
